Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement needs a short, auditable summary of the unit-economics assumptions we used in the MAP evaluation plan before we can finalize the purchase order. Specifically we need:

- Tokens per API call (prompt + response) that you used in the evaluation simulations
- Caching/prefetch assumptions and expected hit rates by endpoint
- Batching policy used for peak traffic (micro-batching parameters)
- Any tail-latency or SLO tradeoffs that could affect operational cost

Could you send a one-pager or table we can attach to the contract? We referenced your prefetch sim during the call — if you can send that CSV it would be super helpful.

Thanks Harry — attaching a concise summary and the CSV you referenced. High level answers below; PDF has the numbers formatted for procurement.

Quick summary (baseline evaluation configuration):
- Average tokens per request: prompt ~95 tokens, model response ~220 tokens => ~315 tokens/request
- Evaluation token cost used: $0.0024 per 1k tokens (model + infra blended assumption for Dedicated footprint)
- Effective tokens/$: ~131,250 tokens per $1
- Prefetching: enabled for repeated context (~40% cache hit rate observed in sim for conversational endpoint); prefetched KV cache reduces average model tokens by ~18% for returned responses
- Micro-batching: target micro-batch = 8 requests per GPU RPC; batching reduces per-token inference overhead ~12% at typical concurrency (see batching-profile.txt)
- Tail behavior: 95th pct latency increases when micro-batch >12 or when cache miss spikes >60% — we captured this in the attached sim.

Next steps: Ben and David can add the technical caveats. We can also produce a short table matching your contract SKUs to expected monthly spend under 3 traffic scenarios (low/expected/high) for the MAP.

Attaching: MAP-econ-summary.pdf (summary table), prefetch-sim-results.csv (raw), batching-profile.txt (profiles)

— Tessa
Director, Commercial Ops
Redwood Inference

Harry — adding the technical detail you requested (short form). Quoting Tessa below for context.

On Mon, 10 May 2027 at 10:03, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com> wrote:
> Quick summary (baseline evaluation configuration):
> - Average tokens per request: prompt ~95 tokens, model response ~220 tokens => ~315 tokens/request
> - Evaluation token cost used: $0.0024 per 1k tokens (model + infra blended assumption for Dedicated footprint)

Notes / caveats:
- Tokenization: the 315 avg uses our standard byte-pair tokenization on the evaluation prompts; if your pre-processing strips metadata you may see -8% tokens/request.
- Caching details: prefetch uses a prefix-KV cache keyed by conversation id + top-3 recent messages. The sim shows a 40% hit-rate for the triage endpoint but only ~18% for the discovery endpoint (varies by call pattern).
- Batching: micro-batch size of 8 is our recommended default for your throughput profile (observed median QPS in the pilot). If you commit to Reserved (Dedicated) we can increase to 12 for more efficiency during stable traffic windows.
- Cost sensitivity: moving batch size from 8=>12 yields ~6–9% tokens/$ improvement; increasing cache hit by +20pp yields ~10–13% improvement.
- Implementation note: to realize batching gains you need to accept up to ~25ms additional tail latency in the worst case for the triage flow — we flagged this in the MAP as an opt-in performance/cost tradeoff.

If Procurement wants a single-line cert for the contract I can provide: "Numbers reflect Redwood evaluation profile v1.2 — avg 315 tokens/request, baseline effective tokens per dollar 131k; batching and prefetch assumptions included in attached simulations."

—Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer

Thanks — this is exactly what we needed. A few follow-ups from Procurement:

- Can you add the official Deal ID and the exact table that maps forecasted monthly QPS to estimated monthly spend (low/med/high)? Procurement wants to attach that table to the PO.
- We prefer min-batch of 6 max-batch 12 in the contract language with a note that Redwood will target batch=8 for expected loads.
- Please confirm whether the $0.0024/1k tokens figure assumes any additional charge for prefetching cache storage or network egress.

We'd like to lock this into the MAP by COB Wednesday. Could you confirm by EOD today whether Redwood will include a small SLA credit (one-time) if realized 95th pct latency exceeds the MAP SLO during the first 30 days of pilot? Procurement would like that as a safety valve.

—Harry

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>

Harry — finalizing the ask; putting the cert table inline for quick copy/paste into your PO. See below and the attached PDF for the full scenarios.

Draft certification table (monthly estimates, USD):
- Low (10k requests/day avg): 10k * 30 * 315 tokens = 94,500,000 tokens => $226.80/month
- Expected (50k requests/day avg): 50k * 30 * 315 = 472,500,000 tokens => $1,134.00/month
- High (150k requests/day avg): 150k * 30 * 315 = 1,417,500,000 tokens => $3,402.00/month

Assumptions / clarifications:
- Deal ID: ACM-2027-0421 (please reference in PO)
- Pricing note: $0.0024 per 1k tokens is a blended unit used for MAP evaluation and includes model + infra; there is no separate line item for prefetch cache storage or egress at the committed tiers in this deal.
- Batching: contract language can read "min-batch 6 / target 8 / max-batch 12"; Redwood will default to target=8 operationally.
- SLA credit: Redwood agrees to include a one-time credit equal to 5% of the first month committed spend if realized 95th pct latency for the primary triage endpoint exceeds the MAP SLO more than 3x in the first 30 days — limited to the committed monthly amount. We can formalize the exact SLA language in the SOW.

Next steps (action items):
- Tessa: attach the signed MAP appendix and updated pricing table to the HubSpot deal (link below).
- Ben: confirm any tokenization caveats in the SOW appendix (if you want tighter guarantees).
- Harry / Procurement: confirm you want us to include the one-time SLA credit clause in the SOW so Legal can draft.

HubSpot: https://hubspot.example/ACM-12345
